message: The Titanic data has a binary target (Survived) with moderate class balance. Key risks are missing values in Age (≈20%) and Cabin (≈77%), and high‑cardinality strings: Name (unique per row), Ticket (681 unique), Cabin (147 unique). To capture useful signal while avoiding over‑fit, we extract structured parts with regexes: Title from Name, CabinLetter from Cabin, and TicketPrefix from Ticket. These low‑cardinality categories can be frequency‑encoded and also used for group target encoding because the same prefix or cabin letter appears across multiple passengers and also in the test set (test_seen_pct > 0 for Cabin and Ticket). We drop the raw high‑cardinality columns after extraction. Age missingness is handled by an indicator (default). Fare is heavily right‑skewed (skew = 4.79) so we log‑transform it. A simple ratio Fare/Age may capture per‑person cost. Group size columns for the extracted keys give the count of passengers sharing the same ticket prefix or cabin letter, which can be predictive. No datetime fields exist. The plan follows the schema and addresses the listed risks.
